summary:
Plan of w130 (work-queue r22 work start, r23 initiative done) written as far as it goes, in plan.md.
Decided: initiative id i<n>, numbered one above the highest (by analogy with work-items-named-by-ids). Fields: kind, status proposed, fulfils the request id, the request's source, title, date. start refuses a missing or non-accepted request (r7) and does not commit (r9 does not name it).
r23 check (new workqueue_done.py): at least one work-item, all green or withdrawn, every request this context asked (asker internal or this context's id) that names the initiative in part_of or source is delivered. Only the status line is written, and initiative.md joins the command's commit (forced by r9's withdraw row).
Open: whether `work run`'s green move counts as a `work` command. Reading A breaks the accepted supervision scenarios at features/supervision.feature:142-148 and :159-164, which are read-only here. Reading B leaves an initiative finished by work run not done.
supervise.py is in the file set only under reading A.
questions: Does `work run` count as 'a `work` command' under work-queue#r23, so that its move of an initiative's last work-item to green sets the initiative to done? Reading A, yes: after `work run i1` takes i1's last work-item to green (and no request this context asked naming i1 is undelivered), .shop/work/i1/initiative.md gives status done, committed with the work-item. The accepted supervision scenarios at features/supervision.feature:142-148 ('.shop/work/i1/initiative.md is as it was') and :159-164 ('as that session committed them') then fail and must be re-formulated before this work-item can go green. Reading B, no: only `work withdraw`, `work retry` and `work answer` set done. After `work run` greens the last work-item, initiative.md stays started, and no later command makes the condition true, because it already holds. The narrator would see such an initiative never become done unless its last change is a withdraw, retry or answer. No supervision test breaks.
